etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Back-formation from ambivalence, from German Ambivalenz, from Latin ambi- (“in two ways”) + valeō (“be strong”); equivalent to ambi- +‎ -valent. Compare ambivert.
senses: Simultaneously experiencing or expressing opposing or contradictory feelings, beliefs, motivations, or meanings.
Alternately being or having one opinion or feeling, and then the opposite.
